description: Compact feed of currently active NasDecode Market Watch catalysts.

activeEvents.companyMarket: U.S. Congress / fiscal policy / Treasuries / Nasdaq / SOX
activeEvents.headline: Reuters reports Democrats capture both chambers of U.S. Congress in 2026 midterm elections
activeEvents.whyItMatters: Control of both congressional chambers changes the legislative balance for the remainder of President Trump's term. Fiscal spending, taxes, trade/export-control oversight and regulatory negotiations could affect Treasury yields and technology valuations; specific policy changes are not yet enacted.

activeEvents.companyMarket: Oracle (ORCL) / Tencent / Nvidia AI chips / China export controls
activeEvents.headline: FT reports Oracle canceled estimated $7B Tencent AI-chip leasing deal after U.S. pressure; Reuters could not independently verify
activeEvents.direction: Negative for reported contract economics; mixed for broader AI supply chain
activeEvents.scope: AI infrastructure / semiconductor export controls / cloud leasing
activeEvents.whyItMatters: The reported cancellation of a five-year lease covering access to roughly 100,000 advanced AI chips at Southeast Asian data centers would constrain a major overseas route for Chinese AI computing and remove a potential multi-billion-dollar Oracle cloud contract. It extends the China-access risk beyond direct semiconductor exports to cloud capacity leasing, with possible implications for Nvidia accelerator demand and regional data-center financing. This is an unconfirmed media report, not an Oracle or U.S. government announcement.

activeEvents.companyMarket: Super Micro Computer (SMCI) / Nvidia AI servers / AI infrastructure
activeEvents.headline: Super Micro beats fiscal Q1 estimates and raises FY2027 sales outlook as AI server demand accelerates
activeEvents.whyItMatters: Fiscal Q1 revenue of $19.95B exceeded LSEG consensus of $16.39B; adjusted EPS $1.81 exceeded $1.23. Fiscal Q2 revenue guidance of $19.5B–$21.5B exceeded $17.14B consensus, while FY2027 guidance rose to $72B–$82B from $65B–$72B. The result provides downstream confirmation of AI rack/server deployment demand and Nvidia-powered infrastructure purchasing, while export-compliance and financing risks remain.

activeEvents.companyMarket: NVDA / China / AI data-center partners / SOX / Nasdaq
activeEvents.headline: FT reports Nvidia directing data-center partners to reduce exposure to Chinese customers; Reuters unable to verify independently
activeEvents.direction: Mixed to negative risk; unconfirmed report
activeEvents.scope: Semiconductor supply chain / US-China technology restrictions
activeEvents.whyItMatters: If substantiated, supplier/customer diversification away from China could alter Nvidia's AI infrastructure distribution and revenue exposure, and intensify geopolitical segmentation of semiconductor supply chains. This is a media report based on unnamed sources, not a confirmed Nvidia directive or new government export-control rule.

activeEvents.companyMarket: U.S. / Iran / Strait of Hormuz / Brent / WTI / Treasury yields / Nasdaq
activeEvents.headline: Reuters reports WSJ account of U.S. strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island; oil edges up after Monday's sharp decline
activeEvents.direction: Negative risk; immediate oil response modest
activeEvents.whyItMatters: Reported renewed U.S. military action near Hormuz threatens the durability of U.S.-Iran negotiations and could restore energy-supply risk premia after Monday's oil selloff. Sustained higher oil could worsen inflation expectations and Treasury discount-rate pressure on Nasdaq and SOX. The strikes are reported rather than independently confirmed by this research; no infrastructure disruption is established.

activeEvents.headline: Palantir reports Q3 revenue up ~96% to $2.31B and guides Q4 above estimates, but US commercial contract-value growth slows to 11%
activeEvents.scope: Mega-cap adjacent AI software / Nasdaq sentiment
activeEvents.whyItMatters: Palantir's strong AI-driven revenue contrasts with sharply slowing US commercial total contract value growth from more than 153% in the prior quarter to 11%, highlighting investor sensitivity to forward bookings and duration of AI contracts despite headline earnings beats.

activeEvents.companyMarket: Lattice Semiconductor (LSCC) / FPGA / AI server infrastructure / SOX
activeEvents.headline: Lattice reports record $291M Q3 revenue (+118% y/y), FPGA sales up ~90%, and guides Q4 revenue to $325M–$345M
activeEvents.whyItMatters: Record results and accelerating FPGA demand from AI servers provide direct evidence of broader AI data-center semiconductor spending. However, year-over-year comparisons include AMI acquired July 2026, so the 118% reported revenue growth must not be interpreted as organic FPGA growth.
